recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not restore the old reasonCode/reasonReference wording in current core Procedure because those elements no longer exist and the current CodeableReference-specific text is governed by the later FHIR-32510 decision.
issue_request: FHIR-16346 was a Published/Persuasive STU3 Patient Care request to clarify when Procedure.reasonCode versus Procedure.reasonReference should be used and whether both could be used. The approved resolution said the two separate elements were not duplicative: a code can summarize the reason, a reference can carry a more precise resource, and both can be used when they describe different reasons for the procedure.
initial_application: Commit 2abadfb0e67fcff244d11e84699e185273719afa applied GF#13974 and GF#16346 in 2018 by adding the requested comments to the then-authoritative Procedure spreadsheet source. That source was later replaced by the current StructureDefinition XML during R5/R6 source refactoring.
additional_context: Current Procedure is active in source/fhir.ini and no longer has separate reasonCode and reasonReference elements. The R5/R6 model uses Procedure.reason of type CodeableReference, with concept and reference facets. Later Published issue FHIR-32510 corrected the migrated wording because both concept and reference in a single CodeableReference must be consistent with each other, not describe different reasons.
reconciliation: The current source/procedure/structuredefinition-Procedure.xml comment already tells implementers to use Procedure.reason.concept when a code is sufficient, Procedure.reason.reference when a referenced resource conveys more information such as onset date, and to keep both facets consistent when they appear in the same Procedure.reason. An empty no-change audit commit was published on the combined branch.

related_jiras.note: Earlier Procedure reasonCode/reasonReference clarification applied in the same 2018 commit and carried into the same historical comments.
Published R5 clarification that superseded the migrated FHIR-16346 wording for CodeableReference by requiring concept and reference in a single Procedure.reason to be consistent.
